version.changelog: Sync skill instructions, references, and helper from GitHub 4164b4f6c8272e152ee99cbafd3d88b4549533e3

llm.summary: This skill appears benign because it uses a disclosed Crawlora API helper to compare public app privacy disclosures and shows no hidden persistence, destructive behavior, or privilege escalation.

dimensions.detail: External API use and a Crawlora API key are proportionate to the stated workflow; the helper fixes the API base URL, rejects unsupported methods, and avoids reading local files through query arguments.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package includes a bundled shell helper for Crawlora access; it is disclosed in SKILL.md and restricts calls to GET requests against an allowlisted route catalog.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions bound collection to the requested scope and credit budget, preserve source context, and explicitly warn against overclaiming runtime privacy or safety conclusions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background workers, system hooks, sudo/root use, destructive commands, or credential-store access were found; chmod 600 only restricts a temporary curl config file containing the API header.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose is coherent: compare App Store privacy labels, Google Play data-safety declarations, and Android permissions for user-selected apps using documented Crawlora endpoints.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, understand that app search terms, app identifiers, storefront/language parameters, and your Crawlora API key will be sent to Crawlora. Use it for public disclosure comparison, not as proof of actual runtime app behavior or device safety, and keep requests within the app set and budget you intend.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The shell helper is a disclosed fallback for Crawlora access; while explicit tool-scope metadata would improve packaging clarity, the artifact constrains the helper to the documented route set.
[E1] expected: Transmission to https://api.crawlora.net/api/v1 is central to the skill and is disclosed alongside the required x-api-key header; no unrelated destination or covert data flow was found.
[PE2] unexpected: The cited chmod 600 line does not invoke sudo or root privileges; it narrows permissions on a temporary curl config file and is not privilege escalation.
[SQP-3] expected: The US/English values appear as optional API defaults and examples, while SKILL.md tells the agent to establish storefront and language before interpreting results, so this is not a forced locale policy in the skill instructions.
